decision: Use a bounded length-prefixed JSON protocol over inherited stdin/stdout as the first Qubes worker transport boundary, with no network listener in DIG

evaluatedApproaches.name: qrexec-style-stdio-length-prefixed-json
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: preserves exact message boundaries across arbitrary stream chunking and composes with the existing HMAC/counter envelope
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: rejects oversized, truncated, malformed, and non-object frames; isolates request failures so one rejected mission does not kill the session
evaluatedApproaches.latency: one four-byte header plus JSON serialization; negligible relative to inter-VM execution
evaluatedApproaches.resourceUse: low and bounded per frame with a 1 MiB default limit
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: low because it wraps AuthenticatedCoordinator.handle without changing queue/auth semantics
evaluatedApproaches.qa: tests cover byte-by-byte chunking, sequential requests, oversized/truncated frames, malformed JSON, and per-request failure isolation

evaluatedApproaches.name: newline-delimited-json-over-stdio
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: simple but newline framing is easier to mishandle when payload generation or diagnostics accidentally write to the transport stream
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: weaker framing discipline and more sensitive to stray stdout output
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: low implementation complexity but weaker boundary guarantees

evaluatedApproaches.name: http-network-listener
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: mature request semantics but introduces a new reachable service and network policy surface
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: requires TLS, bind/firewall policy, certificate lifecycle, and listener hardening
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: high before the real Qubes topology is fixed
evaluatedApproaches.qa: rejected for the current stage because DIG should not open a network listener by default

evaluatedApproaches.name: unix-domain-socket
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: does not itself solve cross-Qube transport and adds socket lifecycle/permission handling
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: medium because an adapter is still required at the Qubes boundary
evaluatedApproaches.qa: deferred as an optional local adapter

whyItWon: It creates the narrowest transport surface for Qubes integration: DIG inherits streams supplied by the Qubes service mechanism instead of binding a port, keeps authentication/replay fencing in the existing protocol layer, enforces bounded deterministic framing, and has very small runtime and regression cost.
knownFailuresAndLessons: This module is transport framing, not a substitute for Qubes qrexec policy. The operator must still define which source Qubes may invoke the service.
Confidentiality depends on the trusted inter-VM mechanism supplying stdin/stdout; DIG does not add application-layer encryption in this adapter.
Anything writing diagnostics to the same stdout stream can corrupt framing; production launchers must reserve stdout exclusively for protocol frames and send logs elsewhere.
A 1 MiB frame cap limits memory-amplification risk but mission payloads should remain substantially smaller and bulk artifacts should use a separate controlled channel.
Per-request errors are intentionally sanitized to code/message and never include stack traces.

REAL-WORKER readiness still requires an actual Qubes qrexec service/policy deployment, worker-side client adapter, restart/partition fault injection across separate Qubes, secret provisioning/rotation, and side-effect idempotency/fencing.
